record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one design efficient algorithms for solving periodic linear matrix inequalities (LMIs)?

evidence.quote: Moreover, there exist no efficient algorithms to solve periodic linear matrix inequalities (LMIs).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system

  x(k+1) = A(k) x(k) + B(k) u(k),    A(k+P) = A(k),  B(k+P) = B(k),

with period P ≥ 1. A periodic linear matrix inequality (periodic LMI) is a finite collection of constraints of the form

  F_0(k) + Σ_{i=1}^{m} x_i(k) F_i(k) ≻ 0,    k = 0, 1, …, P − 1,

where for each k the symmetric matrices F_i(k) ∈ S^{n×n} are given P-periodic data, and the unknowns are P-periodic symmetric matrix variables X(k) = X(k+P) (or, equivalently, scalar decision variables x_i(k)) coupled across k by the periodic system dynamics (typical examples include periodic Lyapunov inequalities A(k)ᵀ X(k+1) A(k) − X(k) + Q(k) ≺ 0 with X(k) = X(k+P) ≻ 0, and their Bounded Real / KYP-type variants).

Problem. Design numerically efficient algorithms that solve such periodic LMIs by exploiting the periodic structure (rather than lifting the system to a single, large time-invariant LMI of dimension proportional to P), with computational cost and storage scaling favorably in the period P and the state dimension n, and with provable numerical stability. In particular, give an algorithm that:

(i) decides feasibility of the periodic LMI system above;
(ii) when feasible, produces a P-periodic symmetric solution X(0), …, X(P−1);
(iii) avoids forming the lifted block-diagonal LMI of size nP × nP whenever possible, and admits structure-preserving (e.g., periodic Schur / periodic QZ based) implementations.

Prove convergence and analyze the per-iteration complexity of the proposed algorithm.
artifact.status_search_result: While LMI-based formulations for discrete-time periodic systems have been studied and certain periodic problems (e.g., periodic Riccati equations, periodic Lyapunov equations) have dedicated structure-exploiting algorithms, no general-purpose efficient solver tailored to periodic LMIs that avoids lifting to a large time-invariant LMI appears to have been established. The standard approach remains lifting plus general interior-point methods, which is acknowledged as inefficient for large period P. No definitive resolution of the open problem was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Linear Matrix Inequalities in System and Control Theory
status_evidence.snippet: There are efficient numerical methods to determine whether an LMI is feasible or to solve a convex optimization problem with LMI constraints.
status_evidence.claim: General LMIs admit efficient interior-point solvers, but no specialized periodic-LMI solver is described.

status_evidence.title: On the algorithms for solving discrete periodic Riccati equation
status_evidence.snippet: Based on the linear matrix inequalities, an algorithm is proposed for constructing the stabilizing solution of discrete periodic Riccati equations.
status_evidence.claim: Specialized algorithms exist for periodic Riccati equations via LMIs, but only in restricted settings.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of discrete-time linear periodic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses analysis methods for discrete-time periodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments rely on lifting; no general efficient periodic LMI solver is highlighted.
